newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Japan said to want crime on APEC agenda.
newsitem.headline: Japan said to want crime on APEC agenda.

text.p: Japan proposed on Friday that transnational crime be considered as a subject for discussion among Pacific Rim nations, a senior Philippine official said.
The suggestion was made during bilateral talks on the APEC sidelines between Philippine Foreign Minister Domingo Siazon, Japanese Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda and Trade Minister Shinji Sato.

Among issues of interest to Japan was "possibly the expansion of the scope of APEC to include new areas of discussion, transnational crimes, for example, commercial crimes, drug smuggling etc," Philippine Foreign Affairs Undersecretary Rodolfo Severino told a news briefing.
The ministers are in Manila for the annual meeting of the 18-member Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum.

APEC members are Australia, Brunei, Canada, Chile, China, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Japan, Malaysia, Mexico, New Zealand, Papua New Guinea, the Philippines, Singapore, South Korea, Taiwan, Thailand and the United States.
